newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics Q2 gross margins rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics Q2 gross margins rise.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp said Wednesday gross margins in its fiscal second quarter increased to 49.1 percent of net sales from 41.9 percent last year.
"The increase was due in part to strong margins on initial shipments of the company's x2 native desktop modem products," the company said in a statement.
The x2 technology allows Internet connections at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second, or roughly twice as fast as today's standard modems, over conventional telephone lines.
Reductions in manufacturing costs and changes in the mix of products sold also pushed gross margins higher, U.S. Robotics said.
Gross margins for the company's first fiscal quarter were 42.8 percent of net sales.

"Although gross margins increased 6.3 percentage points (from first quarter) during the March quarter, the company expects gross margins to return over time to levels more consistent with the company's results in recent quarters," U.S. Robotics said.

U.S. Robotics reported earnings for its second quarter ended March 31 of $0.95 a share including a tax benefit of $0.18 a share. Without the gain, the company earned $0.77 a share. Last year, U.S. Robotics posted second quarter profits of $0.55 a share.
Chief operating officer John McCartney said demand remains strong for computer modems and hubs, used by online service providers, as well as its PC cards and PalmPilot handheld organizers.

"Demand continues to be strong for our expanding portfolio of information access products," McCartney said. "In addition, our x2 technology is available now and is expected to have a widespread impact on Internet users by enabling them to have a more satisfying online experience."
U.S. Robotics began shipping its x2 desktop computer modems in February and the hub technology in March.
McCartney added he expects demand for all U.S. Robotics' product lines to grow during the remainder of the company's fiscal year, as worldwide requirements for information access products increases.
U.S. Robotics said it expects to complete its merger with 3Com Corp in June 1997, and does not expect to report separate results for the June quarter.
In February, 3Com agreed to acquire U.S. Robotics for 1.75 3Com shares per U.S. Robotics share.
